posts.raw_content:
In his 1970 lectures on Islamic Government (Velayat-e Faqih), Khomeini stated: "Monarchy and hereditary succession represent the same sinister, evil system of government that prompted the Lord of the Martyrs (Hussain bin Ali) to rise up in revolt."

These statements were central to his ideology leading up to the 1979 'Islamic Revolution'. He viewed the title of "King" as hated by God and considered hereditary rule a "Pagan" institution adopted from pre-Islamic empires. Iran in 1979 did not call it the 'Iranian Revolution' instead extending it to all of Islam...

By explicitly naming it the "Islamic Revolution" rather than the "Iranian Revolution," Ayatollah Ruhollah Khomeini intentionally framed the event as a Universal Model for all of Islam, not just a National uprising for Iran to overthrow the Shah.

He effectively declared War on Islam seeking to supplant and overthrow it with his own vision of Islam...effectively ending over a thousand years of Dynastic Rule in 'Persia and Arabia'

Among the current Monarchies in the Islamic world, all are Sunni-led, with no existing Shia Monarchies.  The ruling families of these Nations adhere to Sunni Islam, even in cases where the general population may have a large Shia contingent.

Current Islamic monarchies include:

- Bahrain (King Hamad bin Isa Al Khalifa), 
- Brunei (Sultan Hassanal Bolkiah), 
- Jordan (King Abdullah II), 
- Kuwait (Emir Mishal Al Sabah),
- Malaysia (King Abdul Halim),
- Morocco (King Mohammed VI),
- Oman (Sultan Haitham bin Tariq Al Said),
- Qatar (Emir Tamim bin Hamad Al Thani),
- Saudi Arabia (King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud),
- United Arab Emirates (a Federation of seven Emirates ruled by the Al Nahyan, Al Maktoum, Al Qasimi, Al Mualla, and Al Sharqi families). 

Iran's Twelver Shia has placed IRGC and Quds Force controlled Insurgents in many (if not all) Muslim Countries with moderate success in destabilizing their Governments in favor of Iran's version of 'Islam'.  Approximately 80 percent of Islam is Sunni not Shia and their disagreements on Islam date back to the death of Muhammad originating from a succession dispute over who should lead the Muslim community (the Ummah).  This political disagreement eventually hardened into the two main branches of Islam: Sunni and Shia.   

I gotta think those Hereditary Monarchies 'disagree' with Iran's vision for the future of their countries.
